deep.reconstruction:
Context: this folio is a draft of §4 of Riemann's 1851 Göttingen dissertation, 'Grundlagen für eine allgemeine Theorie der Functionen einer veränderlichen complexen Grösse'. The previous page completes the derivation of the Cauchy–Riemann equations. Writing (du + i dv)/(dx + i dy) as [(u_x + i v_x) dx + (v_y − i u_y) i dy]/(dx + i dy), the quotient is independent of the direction dy/dx exactly when u_x = v_y and v_x = −u_y. These are stated to be necessary and sufficient for w = u + iv to be a function of z = x + iy, in Riemann's sense of a complex-differentiable dependence.

This page draws the consequence for each 'Glied' (the real part u and the imaginary part v taken separately): Δu = u_xx + u_yy = 0 and Δv = v_xx + v_yy = 0.

Implicit derivation (my filling, certain):
(1) Differentiate u_x = v_y with respect to x, giving u_xx = v_yx.
(2) Differentiate u_y = −v_x with respect to y, giving u_yy = −v_xy.
(3) Add the two. If the mixed partials are equal (v_xy = v_yx), then u_xx + u_yy = 0.
(4) Similarly, differentiate v_x = −u_y with respect to x and v_y = u_x with respect to y. This gives v_xx + v_yy = −u_yx + u_xy = 0.

Riemann then announces the programme: these Laplace equations are the foundation for studying the properties that belong to one component of a complex function considered by itself. Proving those properties will occupy him next. In the dissertation this is the Dirichlet-principle / boundary-value approach of §§5ff.

The rest of the page is blank. The faint mirrored writing is bleed-through from the recto (the text of the previous page), not new content.
errors: Unstated assumption: passing from Cauchy–Riemann to Laplace requires u and v to be twice differentiable with equal mixed partials (e.g. C^2). Riemann tacitly assumes this, as in the published dissertation. It is in fact true for holomorphic functions, but that is proved only later via Cauchy's integral formula or Riemann's own regularity arguments.

results.what: Real and imaginary parts of a complex-differentiable function each satisfy the 2D Laplace equation (are harmonic), derived from the Cauchy–Riemann equations
results.modern_name: Harmonicity of the real and imaginary parts of a holomorphic function
results.usually_credited_to: Implicit in d'Alembert/Euler (18th c.) and Cauchy (1814/1825); systematically exploited as the foundation of function theory by Riemann (1851 dissertation)

results.what: Programme: base the theory of complex functions on the potential-theoretic properties of a single real component
results.modern_name: Riemann's geometric/potential-theoretic approach to complex analysis (leading to the Dirichlet principle)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft of a passage that appears almost verbatim in §4 of Riemann's published 1851 dissertation. The content (Cauchy–Riemann implies Laplace) is classical and well documented as part of Riemann's work.
